dedupe_keys.name: global renewables watch global temporal dataset of solar pv farms and onshore wind turbines from satellite imagery 2017 q4 to 2024 q2

description: Global Renewables Watch is a global temporal dataset of commercial solar photovoltaic farms and onshore wind turbines, made by Microsoft AI for Good researchers with The Nature Conservancy. Deep learning segmentation models were trained on OpenStreetMap labels and run on PlanetScope imagery at 4.7 m per pixel, over 13 trillion pixels, quarterly from the fourth quarter of 2017 to the second quarter of 2024. The final dataset has 375,197 wind turbines as points and 86,410 solar PV installations as polygons, each with an estimated construction quarter, the preceding ESA CCI land cover class and an ISO3 country code, plus area for solar. Country-level capacity estimates correlate with IRENA 2023 figures with R-squared of 0.96 for solar and 0.93 for wind. The 2024 Q2 solar and wind layers are available to download free as GeoPackage files from the GitHub release, with pre-trained models and inference code, and are also mirrored as Earth Engine feature collections in the community catalogue; the licence is MIT. Coverage is global. Caveats: rooftop solar and offshore wind are outside scope, capacity per site is not given, and construction dates are quarter estimates. Simulation uses are locating wind and solar assets for hazard exposure and for building generation fleets where national registries are missing. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
